papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, delivering flickering light stimulation (FLS) during sleep deprivation prevented the upregulation of activity-dependent and unfolded protein response (UPR)/ER-stress genes while further increasing NREM slow-wave activity, and induced brief neuronal OFF periods resembling a sleep-like cortical state. The authors conclude that physiological manipulation of cortical activity can dissociate ER-stress molecular signatures from electrophysiological markers of sleep pressure.

papers.title: Isoflurane anesthesia CNS recovery state: ultra-slow oscillations and cellular-stress-responsive gene expression
papers.summary: Compared recovery from 4 h isoflurane anesthesia with time-matched sleep and sleep deprivation in male C57BL/6J mice using EEG/EMG and frontal cortex RNA sequencing; isoflurane recovery produced rebound arousal, fragmented NREM, and persistent ultra-slow EEG oscillations normalizing within two weeks. Transcriptomics showed isoflurane and sleep deprivation induced largely distinct cortical programs, with isoflurane enriching integrated stress response and unfolded protein response genes while sleep deprivation showed an mTOR-associated growth-permissive profile.

papers.title: An acetylcholine-inhibited sleep-active hippocampal interneuron orchestrates memory consolidation.
papers.summary: The authors identified a sparse population of Chrm2-expressing (acetylcholine-inhibited) GABAergic interneurons in mouse hippocampus preferentially active during NREM sleep and quiet wakefulness, which inhibited the hippocampus at an infra-slow (~0.015 Hz) rhythm and bidirectionally modulated ripple occurrence. Suppressing these neurons in dorsal CA3 or ventral hippocampus impaired spatial and social memory, respectively, linking neuromodulatory state to ripple-gated memory consolidation.

papers.title: Correction: Cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (CIRBP) adjusts clock-gene expression and REM-sleep recovery following sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: Published erratum correcting the eLife article on cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (CIRBP) regulation of clock-gene expression and REM-sleep recovery after sleep deprivation; no abstract or findings are supplied.

papers.title: Circadian and Sleep-Wake Modulation of EEG Functional Connectivity Across Brain States and Its Associations With Cognition in Humans.
papers.summary: Using over 1,200 hours of artifact-free EEG from a 10-day forced-desynchrony protocol, the study showed that sleep-wake history and circadian phase both modulate EEG functional connectivity, with sleep-wake history having broader influence. Global connectivity rose progressively across NREM sleep (especially delta and sigma bands) but declined during REM sleep, and NREM connectivity measures were associated with subsequent cognitive performance.

papers.title: Layer 1 NDNF interneurons form distinct subpopulations with opposite activation patterns during sleep in freely behaving mice
papers.summary: Used simultaneous cell-specific calcium imaging and local field potential recordings in freely moving mice to examine layer 1 NDNF interneurons during NREM sleep, finding three distinct populations with stage-tuned activity. REM-active L1 NDNF cells inhibited the network at sharp-wave ripple onset depending on spindle coupling, largely via GABAB receptors, suggesting a role in gating SWR-spindle information transfer.

papers.title: Global Time-Aware Conditioning (GTC): A Mechanism for Time-Aware Pediatric Sleep Representation Learning
papers.summary: The authors introduce Global Time-Aware Conditioning (GTC), a mechanism that conditions latent representations in sleep self-supervised learning on each window's global time-of-sleep, complementing local positional encodings. Integrated into three SSL frameworks and evaluated on five clinically relevant tasks across two pediatric cohorts, GTC generally improved F1 and AUPRC, with gains persisting under cross-cohort transfer.

papers.title: Behavioral, Transcriptomic, and Neuroinflammatory Effects of Sleep Deprivation: Insights From Separate Acute and Chronic Experimental Paradigms.
papers.summary: In male C57BL/6J mice, acute 6-h sleep deprivation alleviated despair-like behavior in a pain-depression model while chronic 14-day sleep deprivation induced anxiety- and despair-like behavior. Transcriptomic profiling of five cortical regions implicated the prefrontal cortex (notably Plin4 and Sult1a1), and multiple inflammatory cytokines decreased after acute but increased after chronic sleep deprivation.

papers.title: SleepPairNet: Learning Multimodal Pediatric Sleep Representations with Random-Pair Cross-Attention
papers.summary: The authors present SleepPairNet, a multimodal self-supervised learning framework that uses random modality-pair selection and cross-attention to learn pairwise interactions among physiological sleep signals. Pretrained on the NCH dataset, it outperformed evaluated SSL baselines on all respiratory tasks, remained competitive on EEG tasks, and transferred even more strongly to the external CHAT dataset.

papers.title: Phasic pupil responses to melanopsin- and cone-directed stimulation remain stable across circadian time
papers.summary: Using a 40-hour ultra-short sleep-wake protocol with silent-substitution pupillometry in healthy adults, the authors tested whether phasic pupil responses to melanopsin- and cone-directed stimuli vary with circadian phase. Hierarchical cosinor comparisons favored constant-level over circadian models for phasic amplitude across all five stimulus conditions, not supporting circadian modulation under the tested parameters.

papers.title: Sleep stage-specific heart rate variability feature-driven clustering analysis: identifying cardiac autonomic endotypes with long-term cardiovascular predictive value.
papers.summary: In 4029 Sleep Heart Health Study participants, the authors applied stage-specific (N2, N3, REM) linear and non-linear HRV features with K-means clustering to derive three phenotypes (Stable, Burden, High risk). The High-risk phenotype was consistently associated with increased incident cardiovascular disease across sleep stages (e.g., N2 HR 1.468, 95% CI 1.280-1.684), with minimal attenuation after adjusting for AHI, ODI, arousal index, and sleep efficiency.

papers.title: Sleep Stage Classification Across Heterogeneous EEG/EOG Channels with Multi-channel Differential Transformer.
papers.summary: Proposes SleepDIFFormer, a multi-channel differential transformer framework with cross-domain alignment for heterogeneous EEG/EOG representation learning, trained across multiple sleep-staging datasets as source domains. It achieved superior performance versus existing approaches on five datasets under domain generalization settings, with ablation and attention-weight analyses supporting its discriminative representations.

papers.title: REM Atonia Index Cutoffs for REM Sleep Without Atonia: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis of Adult Diagnostic Performance.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 30 studies found that chin-EMG REM Atonia Index discriminates established REM sleep behavior disorder with pooled sensitivity 0.850 and specificity 0.895, and RAI was lower in RBD by a pooled mean difference of -0.263. However, heterogeneous thresholds (0.80-0.90) and sparse normative data argue against a universal numerical cutoff, supporting continuous reporting of RAI with age-conditioned interpretation.

papers.title: Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome: Unloading the Respiratory System with Expiratory Pressure.
papers.summary: This perspective proposes that abdominal obesity-induced reductions in expiratory reserve volume, functional residual capacity, and end-expiratory lung volume are upstream mechanical abnormalities linking OSA, increased work of breathing, sleep hypoventilation, and daytime hypercapnia in obesity hypoventilation syndrome. Within this framework, CPAP and expiratory positive airway pressure act partly by mechanical unloading through raising end-expiratory lung volume, with weight loss as structural unloading.

papers.title: Nonlinear Feature Modeling Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Electroencephalography for Depression Classification: Deep Learning Study.
papers.summary: The authors introduced Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-based convolutional architectures (ConvKAN and ConvKAN Efficient) for EEG-based depression classification on the EDRA dataset. ConvKAN Efficient achieved the best performance, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score all exceeding 94%, outperforming conventional CNN and traditional machine learning approaches.

papers.title: Three-month follow-up after discontinuation of steam-assisted respiratory muscle training in mild-to-moderate obstructive sleep apnea: an exploratory polysomnographic study.
papers.summary: This exploratory secondary follow-up of a single-arm trial assessed polysomnography in 33 mild-to-moderate OSA patients three months after stopping 12 weeks of steam-assisted respiratory muscle training. No overall visit effect appeared in conventional respiratory-event indices, but N1 proportion and PLMS-related arousal index and count differed across visits, with REM latency differences not robust in sensitivity analyses.

papers.title: Single-Lead EEG-based virtual reality motion sickness detection using interpretable feature selection.
papers.summary: Proposes a SHAP-based single-lead EEG modeling and feature-screening framework for lightweight VRMS detection, selecting FT11 as the optimal lead and achieving 87.53% ± 0.73% accuracy with seven features under window-level tenfold cross-validation. A post hoc LOSO test showed limited cross-subject generalization, which the authors caution is not a fully independent estimate.

papers.title: Considering counterfactual prediction models in sleep research: A demonstration of incident stroke prediction in an observational cohort study.
papers.summary: Applying Model Path Selection to 4512 Sleep Heart Health Study adults to predict 5-year incident stroke, the authors identified 61 unique counterfactual models, 13 of which achieved AUCs between 0.81 and 0.82, all including age plus varying combinations of polysomnography indices, BMI, and SF-36 component scores. The work demonstrates that multiple equally predictive feature sets can exist for the same outcome, informing reproducible and clinically practical risk models.

papers.title: Comparing re-referencing methods for human intracranial EEG
papers.summary: Using intracranial EEG from 16 patients during an episodic memory task, the authors compared multiple re-referencing methods on macro contact and micro-wire data. Re-referencing choice altered artifact-rejection trial proportions, low-frequency power, and the aperiodic background, but in hippocampal recordings no method changed the magnitude or direction of memory effects in power or spike-field coherence.

papers.title: Amplitude-integrated electroencephalogram (aEEG): A bedside window into newborn brain function in the NICU.
papers.summary: This review describes amplitude-integrated EEG as a bedside tool for neonatal brain monitoring in the NICU, emphasizing its practical advantages in assessing hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and first-line seizure detection alongside conventional video EEG. It argues that integrating aEEG within multimodal neuromonitoring enhances neurodevelopmental prognostication and individualized bedside intervention.

papers.title: Composite sleep patterns and the allergy-related composite outcome among American and Chinese older adults: exploration of depressive symptoms as a potential mediator.
papers.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
papers.summary: In NHANES 2005-2006 older adults, poor versus healthy composite sleep was associated with higher odds of an allergy-related composite outcome (OR 2.100), wheeze, and sneeze, with depressive symptoms accounting for an estimated 22.5% of the total association; CHARLS longitudinal analysis linked impaired sleep quality to incident asthma (OR 1.689) with 28.3% mediated through depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 7 studies (3 RCTs, 4 non-randomised; n=390) examined clinical, cognitive, and electrophysiological outcomes of EEG neurofeedback in adult ADHD. RCTs showed small, generally non-significant effects versus controls, while naturalistic and personalised protocols reported large symptom reductions; no treatment-related adverse events occurred.

papers.title: Prebiotics in sport and exercise: current evidence, practical applications, and methodological considerations.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
papers.summary: Narrative review of prebiotic intake in athletic populations, reporting evidence that prebiotics may improve gut barrier integrity, reduce exercise-associated gastrointestinal symptoms, increase salivary IgA secretion rate, and reduce duration/severity of upper respiratory symptoms in trained individuals. It highlights limited high-quality evidence and calls for adequately powered studies with microbiome/metabolome profiling and robust performance measures.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea is frequent in patients with Long COVID fatigue but is not significantly associated with alterations of quality of life and cognition.
papers.summary: Home sleep testing in 100 consecutive Long COVID patients with fatigue but no prior OSA history found OSA in 53% (33% mild, 20% moderate-to-severe). OSA was not significantly associated with Long COVID symptom burden, quality of life, or objective cognitive function, though 20% with moderate-to-severe OSA warrant intervention.

papers.title: Longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and their association with cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity risk in postmenopausal women: evidence from the CHARLS study.
papers.summary: Using 4 repeated sleep measurements (2011-2018) from 2,859 postmenopausal women in CHARLS, group-based trajectory modeling identified normal-stable, normal-fluctuating decline, and short-rapid decline sleep patterns. Relative to normal-stable, the normal-fluctuating decline (OR 2.30) and short-rapid decline (OR 3.75) trajectories independently predicted incident cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity.

papers.title: Comparative effects of exercise modalities on sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders: A systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-responsemeta-analyses.
papers.journal: Journal of exercise science and fitness
papers.summary: This systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-response meta-analyses of 23 RCTs (1,478 middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders) found exercise reduced PSQI and ISI scores but not ESS. Aerobic exercise showed the largest PSQI improvement (SMD 1.34) versus mind-body (0.64) and combined exercise (0.60), with an inverted U-shaped dose-response peaking near 539 MET-min/week.

papers.title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study combined mobile EEG and eye tracking with LabStreamingLayer synchronization during a director-task dyadic communication paradigm, computing regression-based ERPs time-locked to spoken nouns and fixations. Targets competing with occluded referents elicited a stronger posterior positivity, fixation timing modulated neural responses, and established artifact-subspace reconstruction, ICA, and linear deconvolution methods proved applicable to naturalistic datasets.

papers.title: The qualitative exploration of work productivity among chronic rhinitis patients.
papers.summary: Qualitative study combining a literature review with semi-structured interviews of 19 chronic rhinitis patients, using thematic analysis to identify eight themes describing reduced work productivity, including absenteeism, presenteeism, reduced efficiency, sleepiness at work, and workplace stigma. The findings are framed as informing targeted management strategies.

papers.title: Sleep duration and risk of microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes: A prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 1236 adults with type 2 diabetes, both short (<7 h) and long (≥10 h) sleep duration were associated with increased risk of composite microvascular complications (HR=1.71 and HR=1.87, respectively), with a U-shaped dose-response and lowest risk at 7-8 h.

papers.title: Comment on "melatonin and oxidative DNA damage in REM- and NREM-related obstructive sleep apnea: an exploratory analysis of sleep-stage phenotypes".
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This letter comments on a published exploratory analysis of melatonin and oxidative DNA damage in REM- and NREM-related obstructive sleep apnea; it contains no abstract or reported findings of its own.

papers.title: Is Less More? Exploring the Visual Processes of Minimalist and Complex Photography Through Eye Tracking and EEG.
papers.summary: Using eye tracking, consumer-grade EEG, and subjective ratings in 30 participants, the study found that minimalist versus complex photographs produced fewer but longer fixations, more concentrated hotspots, lower perceived complexity, greater relaxation, and higher attention eSense levels, without an aesthetic difference.

papers.title: Mapping mental health complexity in esports: an exploratory psychosocial network approach.
papers.summary: In a 17-item survey of 1025 esports players analyzed with Directed Acyclic Graph network analysis, game-related thought preoccupation emerged as the most robust sink node, with depressed mood upstream, mental fatigue intermediate, and emotion control/autonomy linking affective distress to esports-specific indicators.

papers.title: Enhancement of gut-microbiome-based classification of prodromal Parkinson's Disease cases by hyperparameter tuning, integration of multimodal data, and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This study classified prodromal Parkinson's disease (RBD cases versus controls) from public gut microbiome datasets using batch correction, hyperparameter tuning, multimodal feature integration, and meta-analysis, identifying six depleted short-chain fatty acid-producing genera shared by RBD and PD groups. The tuned model reached an AUC of 0.889, rising to a peak mean AUC of 0.917 when microbial and clinical features were combined, while the six SCFA-producing taxa alone retained a mean AUC of 0.853.

papers.title: Effects of an Esketamine-Containing Induction Regimen on Postoperative Sleep, Analgesia, and Postpartum Depression in Parturients with Sleep Disorders Undergoing Cesarean Section Under General Anesthesia: A Double-Blind Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: In a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial of 90 parturients with preoperative sleep disorders undergoing cesarean section under general anesthesia, an esketamine-containing induction regimen (esketamine 0.25 mg/kg plus propofol 1.0 mg/kg versus saline plus propofol 2.0 mg/kg) significantly improved the primary outcome of sleep NRS on postoperative day 1 (mean difference 3.0, 95% CI 2.0–4.0, P<0.001). Secondary exploratory outcomes suggested early pain benefits and lower continuous EPDS scores on POD 3, but the trial was not powered for secondary or safety outcomes and differing propofol doses prevent isolation of esketamine's specific effect.

papers.title: Effect of a Subanesthetic Dose of Esketamine on Postoperative Sleep Disturbance After Oocyte Retrieval Under Intravenous Anesthesia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 196 women undergoing oocyte retrieval under intravenous anesthesia, a single subanesthetic dose of esketamine 0.2 mg/kg reduced the estimated incidence of postoperative sleep disturbance on POD 3 versus saline (13.06% vs 24.90%; RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.28–0.99; P=0.047), with similar per-protocol results. Postoperative pain at 30 minutes was lower with esketamine, but dreaming was more frequent and time to full alertness and PACU stay were modestly longer.

papers.title: A general condition for fast rates in multi-group learning
papers.summary: The paper identifies a group-wise Bernstein condition under which an adaptive multi-group learning predictor attains fast 1/n rates without prior knowledge of whether the condition holds, while retaining slow rates on groups where it fails, and gives lower bounds and extensions to VC classes.

papers.title: An incidental heterozygous ATP7B nonsense variant leading to a diagnostic pitfall for Wilson disease: a pediatric case report.
papers.summary: A pediatric case report describes a 13-year-old boy with paroxysmal postural instability and dystonic/choreiform movements in whom an incidentally detected heterozygous ATP7B nonsense variant (c.2851C>T; p.Gln951Ter) raised concern for Wilson disease, but normal ceruloplasmin, ceruloplasmin oxidase activity, liver biochemistry, liver ultrasound, and 24-hour urinary copper, plus paternal segregation, made active Wilson disease highly unlikely. The report highlights that interpreting a single heterozygous ATP7B variant outside a compatible phenotype can cause overdiagnosis and diagnostic anchoring bias, emphasizing phenotype-driven evaluation, Leipzig scoring, and biochemical gold standards.

papers.title: MRI Characterization of Structural Brain Abnormalities in NGLY1 Deficiency.
papers.journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
papers.summary: This case series analyzed structural MRI scans from 11 patients with molecularly diagnosed NGLY1 deficiency (ages 2–19 years) and reported significantly reduced subcortical volumes, particularly bilateral thalamus and putamen, with age-dependent cortical alterations including widespread surface area, volume, and curvature reductions in younger patients and thinner dorsal/thicker ventral cortex in older patients. Thalamic volume reduction in older patients correlated with gait disturbance, dysphagia, and EEG abnormalities, suggesting these morphometric measures may serve as biomarkers of disease progression or treatment efficacy.

papers.title: Early Postoperative Psychological Resilience Patterns and Associated Factors in Patients with Knee Stiffness Undergoing Arthroscopic Release Surgery: A Latent Class Growth Model Study.
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 240 patients undergoing arthroscopic release for knee stiffness, latent class growth modeling identified three early postoperative psychological resilience trajectories (Low Declining 17.1%, Moderate Stable 68.8%, High Increasing 14.2%); lower perceived social support and poorer sleep quality were associated with the Low Declining group, and lower education, lower social support, and lower ERRI scores with the Moderate Stable group.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of pain experience and quality of life in patients with oral lichen planus and burning mouth syndrome.
papers.journal: Journal of oral & facial pain and headache
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional comparison of 46 patients with oral lichen planus and 50 with burning mouth syndrome, burning mouth syndrome showed higher pain intensity and catastrophizing, whereas oral lichen planus showed greater mastication-related pain interference and poorer quality of life; regression identified mastication and rumination as predictors in OLP and sleep disturbance, rumination, and magnification in BMS.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
